history.task: Mission Control V0.1 Localization Acceptance Fix (zh-TW / ko / en)
history.summary: Joey's Acceptance Test found one V0.1 requirement: the UI was English-only. A bounded presentation-layer localization fix was implemented for exactly three UI languages — 繁體中文 (zh-TW, default), 한국어 (ko), English (en). Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) was explicitly removed from scope by Joey. No lifecycle logic, canonical parsing, project data, Handoff semantics, or architecture was changed. V0.1 is NOT marked finally accepted.
history.changes:
New files:
`public/i18n.js` — centralized localization module: three dictionaries with identical stable keys, `t(key, params)`, locale persistence (`localStorage` key `mc-locale`, default `zh-TW`, try/catch-safe), render-time label mappers (status, phase, session state, dirty state, provenance classification/verification), exact-match localization of fixed backend messages (embedded technical values preserved), and `applyStaticTranslations` for `data-i18n` / `data-i18n-aria-label` shell elements.
`tests/i18n.test.mjs` — 10 localization regression tests.

Modified files:
`public/index.html` — global language selector in the header (繁體中文 / 한국어 / English); `data-i18n` keys on all shell text; English text kept as no-JS fallback; Inbox type `<option>`s carry canonical `value`s.
`public/app.js` — all chrome rendered via `t()`; canonical values mapped to labels only at render time; filters still compare canonical status values; language switch re-renders the cached snapshot (no API call, no write); Continue result, Inbox preview and status notices re-render on switch.
`public/styles.css` — `.locale-control` layout; `word-break:keep-all` on buttons and table headers (prevents CJK labels breaking per character); mobile-only rule placing the token label on its own row.
`src/server.mjs` — static allowlist adds `i18n.js` (one-word change).
`tests/ui-contract.test.mjs` — existing contract checks now read `app.js` together with `i18n.js`, since UI copy moved into the i18n module; no assertion was weakened or removed.
